extracted.intended_audience: research funders, grant program designers, science policy researchers, and academics interested in research funding systems
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and critique of peer-review-based grant rubrics with a cost-accounting comparison to a universal baseline grant; proposes an alternative, eligibility-based rubric and questions the value of fine-grained ranking. Useful for designing or evaluating funding program rules and allocation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost per failed application
rubrics_metrics.description: The total monetary and time cost attributable to each unsuccessful proposal (Gordon & Poulin estimate ~$40,000 CAD per failed application for NSERC Discovery Grants in 2007).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculated by summing applicant preparation time, reviewer time, administrative overhead, opportunity cost, and resubmission-cycle costs; used to compare against the cost of giving every qualified researcher a baseline grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average baseline discovery grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical amount of a baseline discovery grant (reported as approximately $30,000 CAD in the NSERC 2007 example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the comparator in the cost-accounting argument — if cost per failed application exceeds this amount, a baseline-grant policy could be more efficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant time (proposal preparation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amount of researcher/professor time invested preparing a proposal (estimated at 6–8 weeks of professor time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treated as a measurable cost in evaluating the efficiency of a competitive review system; includes opportunity cost of time away from research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer time (external review and panel discussion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time spent by external reviewers and panel members evaluating proposals and participating in panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the cost calculation for peer review; contributes to administrative and volunteer burden on the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative overhead of running the competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct costs to the funding agency for managing the competition, processing proposals, organizing panels, and related administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the per-proposal cost; reducing administrative complexity is a lever for lowering total system cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity cost of researcher time not spent on research
rubrics_metrics.description: Value of lost research productivity when researchers spend time preparing proposals and participating in review instead of doing research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts as an economic cost when assessing whether competitive review is cost-effective compared to baseline funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: The repeated submission and review rounds many proposals undergo before securing funding (adds cumulative cost across cycles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increases total per-successful-grant system cost; relevant when evaluating the marginal cost of competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding-rate sensitivity (funding rates are too high)
rubrics_metrics.description: When funding rates are high (e.g., NSERC ~70%), fine-grained ranking may add little value because many applicants are similarly qualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should consider whether a rubric that discriminates finely is necessary at high funding rates or whether coarse eligibility would suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marginal-difference justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether marginal differences between proposals justify the time and expense required to distinguish them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A central evaluative question: if marginal quality differences are negligible, costly ranking is less defensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric's administrative-legitimacy function
rubrics_metrics.description: The idea that the rubric may primarily serve administrative legitimacy and signaling rather than allocation efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designers should distinguish procedural/legitimacy goals from allocative goals when choosing rubric complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-proposal effort vs per-grant value for marginal applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: When the effort to prepare and review a marginal applicant's proposal exceeds the expected value of the grant awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If true, the system is inefficient for those marginal cases and may warrant alternative designs (e.g., baseline grants, lotteries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility threshold (proposed alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: A simple pass/fail eligibility criterion determining which investigators qualify for the baseline grant (e.g., 'qualified investigator at a Canadian university').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replaces fine-grained merit ranking with a threshold test; design requires clear, administrable eligibility rules to prevent gaming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard funding amount (proposed alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: A uniform, pre-set grant amount given to all eligible investigators (the 'baseline grant').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplifies allocation and reduces proposal/preparation costs; amount should be set to balance fiscal sustainability and meaningful support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of fine-grained ranking (proposed alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: No review beyond basic eligibility; competitive scoring and detailed ranking are removed for baseline awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shifts allocation from competitive ranking to universality among eligibles; retains potential for separate mechanisms to fund above-baseline work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic continuation review (proposed alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of continued funding eligibility based on past productivity/output rather than new competitive proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides accountability and a means to discontinue support for non-productive awards while avoiding the repeated cost of proposal preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate competitive program for above-baseline funding (proposed alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: A distinct, competitive funding stream reserved for ambitious, high-cost, or high-risk projects above the baseline level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves targeted competition for projects where fine-grained selection adds clear value while keeping baseline funding simple.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marginal value of fine-grained ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: An implication/question for rubric design: what additional benefit does fine-grained ranking provide over simple eligibility or coarse selection?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designers should estimate the incremental scientific or allocative value of fine distinctions and weigh it against the incremental cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost of preparing applications and conducting reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: An explicit design consideration: quantify applicant, reviewer, and administrative costs to determine whether a rubric's complexity is justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robust cost accounting (including opportunity costs and resubmission effects) is required to compare competitive and baseline models fairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation-efficiency justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the rubric's ability to allocate funds better (efficiency) justify its overhead?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubric designers should require evidence that finer-grained allocation materially improves outcomes before incurring substantial process costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified-lottery vs baseline-grant tradeoff
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison between preserving coarse competitive selection (modified lottery) and eliminating competition entirely (baseline grant); both challenge detailed rubrics when ranking validity is limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider hybrid models where merit screening identifies a pool and randomization or baseline funding allocates within or across groups, depending on program goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical defensibility of fine-grained ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Concern about whether fine-grained rankings are statistically reliable, especially given reviewer variability and measurement noise (relevant even in lower funding-rate programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment of rubric reliability and signal-to-noise should inform whether ranking decisions can be justified; low reliability weakens claims for costly discrimination.
